summary.title: TransWeb at a glance
summary.1: A TransWeb digital worker is an AI colleague that runs in the browser: no client to install, no server to prepare — open a page and create one.
summary.2: Going live typically takes about 3 minutes: upload documents or generate a skill from one sentence, compose skills into a workflow, and deliver it with a link or QR code.
summary.3: Pricing is pay-as-you-go: no seat subscriptions, and idle time costs 0.
summary.4: Your materials are isolated per account and never used for public model training; with private deployment and your own models, data can stay entirely inside your intranet.
summary.5: Made for teachers, HR, researchers, consultants, and anyone who needs to turn documents into job-ready capability.
conclusion.title: Conclusion: the browser is the desk, your documents are the job skills.
conclusion.desc: In short, TransWeb compresses building an AI assistant into 3 steps and about 3 minutes: open a page, feed it documents, deliver a link. The online version is pay-as-you-go with zero idle cost; the self-hosted version installs on your own server so data can stay inside your intranet. Teachers, HR, researchers, and consultants can all start with one document today and gain a digital colleague on duty 24/7.

process.title: Three steps to open a desk, then it clocks in.
process.desc: Getting a TransWeb digital worker on the job takes 3 steps: open a page, feed it documents, hand it out — all in the browser, with no client to install and no deployment scripts, typically about 3 minutes to go live.
process.1.title: Open · ready to use
process.1.text: The TransWeb URL is the workspace: creating, previewing, and publishing a digital worker all happen on one page, with no client to install and no server to buy.
process.2.title: Learn · able to work
process.2.text: Upload PDF, Word, or Markdown files, or generate a skill from one sentence and compose skills into a workflow — the digital worker grows job-specific capability around your business.
process.3.title: Work · delivers results
process.3.text: The digital worker researches, runs workflows, and produces conclusions; once delivered by link or QR code, the recipient opens a browser and uses it, while the creator stays away without any downtime.
cases.title: Four kinds of people, one digital team.
cases.desc: TransWeb digital workers currently cover 4 job scenarios: AI teaching assistant (teachers), onboarding mentor (HR), research assistant (researchers and analysts), and domain consultant (service teams). The approach is the same across all four: hand over the material you explain every day, and the digital worker answers from that source material first, ready to be delivered as a link.
case.1.title: AI teaching assistant
case.1.desc: Once teachers hand textbooks, lecture notes, and slides to the AI teaching assistant: when a student asks how to solve a problem, the assistant walks through the source material step by step; when a teacher needs an exam, the assistant writes and grades questions from the knowledge points. One AI assistant, available to the whole class at any time.
case.2.title: Onboarding mentor
case.2.desc: Once HR hands the employee handbook, SOPs, and training material to the onboarding mentor: when a newcomer asks how reimbursement or project approval works, the mentor answers instantly from the policy. New hires take fewer detours, and senior staff no longer act as a human manual.
case.3.title: Research assistant
case.3.desc: Once researchers hand reading notes, industry reports, and excerpts to the research assistant: ask about a report's conclusion and the assistant retrieves it with its source; after a first draft, the assistant continues checking for gaps.
case.4.title: Domain advisor
case.4.desc: Once a service firm hands industry standards, policies, and cases to the domain consultant: when a client asks how to apply for a qualification or what a new rule changes, the consultant quotes the source clause by clause. Account managers no longer dig through files, and both teams and clients can ask directly.

deploy.activate.caption: Configure root access, compute, models, payments, and the login verification code in priority order; expand to review each step.
deploy.activate.root.label: root admin account
deploy.activate.root.overview: Highest priority: get the admin login credentials first, then configure compute, payments, and the login verification code.
deploy.activate.root.desc: transweb root accessKey prints the root admin account and universal verification code. Choose code login and enter the universal code; change the default account and password immediately after first login and never expose initial credentials to the public internet.
deploy.activate.api.label: Compute provider
deploy.activate.api.overview: A compute provider is the channel through which TransWeb reaches large models: one provider maps to one apiName, and private deployment requires at least one.
deploy.activate.api.desc: Compute provider setup defines a custom name and key: apiName is a custom provider name (for example dmxapi, or a name like DeepSeek); models reference it via --api-name. --key is written to .env as API_KEY_*; common.js keeps only a reference.
deploy.activate.model.label: model
deploy.activate.model.overview: A model is the actual large model a digital worker calls: models sit under a compute provider, and at least one must be configured and set as default.
deploy.activate.model.desc: Model configuration defines calling and billing rules: at least one model with apiName, rates, and from. A rate is the credits-to-token ratio — how many credits one AI token costs, billed separately for input and output. from is domestic or overseas; context is the context window size. After configuring, run transweb default model to set it as default.
deploy.activate.pay.label: WeChat Pay
deploy.activate.pay.overview: WeChat Pay is used for credit top-ups: configure APIv2 parameters before taking real payments, completing at least the required fields.
deploy.activate.pay.desc: WeChat Pay setup has required and optional parameter groups. Required: WX_PAY_APP_ID, WX_PAY_MCH_ID, WX_PAY_APP_KEY (32-char APIv2 key), WX_PAY_ORDER_URL, WX_PAY_QUERY_URL. Optional: WX_PAY_APP_SECRET, WX_PAY_NOTIFY, WX_PAY_APP_ID001 / SECRET001. Set values with transweb wxpay set and verify with transweb wxpay check. The install-generated APP_KEY is random; replace it with your merchant APIv2 key before taking payments.
deploy.activate.sms.label: Login verification code
deploy.activate.sms.overview: The SMS verification service powers phone login and registration: without configuration, phone-code login is unavailable.
deploy.activate.sms.desc: SMS verification setup needs just one API key: SEND_MESSAGE_API_KEY (Luosimao SMS), written with transweb env set SEND_MESSAGE_API_KEY <key>. Without it, phone-code login and registration are unavailable.
deploy.activate.hint: Expand each item for commands; check AI config with transweb api list, transweb model list, and transweb default list, WeChat Pay with transweb wxpay check, and SMS with transweb env get SEND_MESSAGE_API_KEY. Add --force to overwrite existing API/model entries. transweb root accessKey and transweb env get read the same .env values for ADMIN_ACCOUNT / POWER_ADMIN; run transweb restart after changing them.
faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.desc: What it is, whether it really works, what you need to install, and how data and billing are handled — the questions we hear most.
faq.q1: What is 'AI digital labor that runs in the browser'?
faq.a1: A digital labor worker refers to an AI colleague that uses the browser as its workspace and completes multi-step tasks by role. No client install or server setup is required — open a web page to create, tune, and deliver one. Unlike a chatbot that only converses, a digital worker reads your uploaded documents, calls skills, and runs 3 kinds of tasks through workflows: research, process execution, and conclusion delivery. Each worker binds 1 document library and several skills, answers primarily from the source material, and acts by role rather than just replying. Once created, deliver it by link or QR code; the recipient opens a browser and uses it without the creator present.
faq.q2: How is it different from a chatbot or an AI agent?
faq.a2: The three differ by capability level: a chatbot only converses, an AI Agent calls tools, and a digital worker is closer to a full job role. A digital worker has 3 components: a persona (role definition), source grounding (a dedicated knowledge base), and skills (executable capabilities). Multiple skills can be composed into a workflow that runs a multi-step process, then delivered to a specific person by link, web page, or QR code. The platform unifies all three as one set of building blocks: the Agent executes, skills are capabilities, and the workflow is the procedure. So the evaluation criterion is not whether it can chat, but whether it can independently deliver results by role.
faq.q3: Do I need to install software or set up a server?
faq.a3: Using the online version requires no software install or server: the browser is the workspace, and all 3 actions — creating, previewing, and publishing a digital worker — happen on a web page. A server is needed in only one case: when an enterprise chooses private deployment, it installs the whole service on its own server with one installer (transweb-service); members still access it via browser, with no client install. In short, individuals and small teams can start with zero deployment, while schools and enterprises use the same capabilities with data staying inside their intranet.
faq.q4: Are my documents used to train models?
faq.a4.1: No. Documents only build your own digital labor; traffic is encrypted over HTTPS and storage is isolated per account. We do not use documents for public model training, and other users cannot search them. You can delete documents at any time, which invalidates the parsed results. See the
compliance.ref1: For data-use standards in generative AI services, see the Interim Measures for the Management of Generative AI Services, issued by seven authorities including the Cyberspace Administration of China (effective 15 August 2023).
faq.a5: Costs are pay-as-you-go, with the core formula: usage billing = model call credits + publish/export service fees, where the publish/export service fee is capped at 10% of the model call credits. Model credits are converted from actual token consumption, billed separately for input and output; publishing or exporting incurs a one-time configured fee. There is no per-seat subscription plan, and idle time costs 0 — you pay for work done, not for seats. Exact amounts follow on-page display and actual account usage, with details always viewable under My Agent / Skill.
faq.q6: What kind of work can it do?
faq.a6: What can a digital worker do? The scope covers 4 categories: answering questions from documents, researching with sources, drafting from materials, and running an order through a workflow — with question generation and grading also supported. Underlying skills can be generated from one sentence, and multiple skills composed into a workflow with human confirmation. Digital workers excel at tasks with source grounding and clear steps; if a result is unsatisfactory, add material or adjust the skill and regenerate instead of starting over.
faq.q7: What if an answer is not accurate?
faq.a7.1: It usually means the documents lack the content or are too fragmented. Add or replace documents and regenerate; mention the chapter or a technical term so it can locate the passage. If the problem persists,
faq.a7.2: with the document type and an example question.
faq.q8: Can I hand it to students, colleagues, or clients?
faq.a8: Yes. There are 3 delivery methods: a one-click link, a QR code, or web embedding. The recipient opens a browser and uses it with no client install; consumption uses their own account and credits, so you do not repeat explanations. All 3 methods point to the same published digital worker — after updating a skill or adding material, the link and QR code reflect the changes without re-delivery.
faq.q9: How do I move a digital worker or AI skill between TransWeb services?
faq.a9: You can move the definition, not the account data. Sign in to the source service and choose Download from the Agent / skill editor menu to get an archive with appCode.vue, appPrompt.md, and manifest.json. Then sign in to the target service, click Clone at the lower right of the input box on the AI Skill Generator page, choose Clone chat Agent or Clone AI skill → Clone from local file, and select appCode.vue (appPrompt.md optional). If the source service is publicly reachable, you can also use Clone from URL with the manifest.json address. Cross-account moves must be exported by the owning account; the target service needs a working API and model first.
faq.q10: After moving, do documents, conversations, credits, and shared links come along?
faq.a10: No. Only the definition files (interface code, prompt, and manifest) travel in the package; documents, knowledge-base results, conversations, credits, accounts, and published links stay on the source service. On the target service you need to upload documents again, rebuild the knowledge base, pick a model, and publish to get a new share link and QR code. The same applies when switching accounts within one service: data and credits stay separate.

legal.accessibility.title: Accessibility statement
a11y.s1.title: Our commitment
a11y.s1.text: This service is for everyone, including people who use screen readers, keyboards, magnification software or voice input. We design to WCAG 2.2 AA and keep checking color contrast, focus order, keyboard operation and text resizing.
a11y.s2.title: What we have done
a11y.s2.text: Every page works with a keyboard. The skip link goes straight to the main content. Body text has a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1. Narrow screens do not need horizontal scrolling. Animations respect the system preference for reduced motion.
a11y.s3.title: Known limitations
a11y.s3.text: On narrow screens the page is scaled to a 480/530px canvas so embedded editors stay usable, which makes some text smaller. Dragging workflow nodes currently needs a mouse or touch screen. Type size, layout and alternative text in the built-in creator and in charts or formulas generated by third-party models depend on those components, so they may not fully follow this site’s standards. We will improve these areas in future releases.
a11y.s4.title: Tell us about your experience
a11y.s4.text: If you cannot use a page or feature, email neilking@163.com with your device, browser and assistive technology. We will reply within 5 working days and give a fix date once we confirm the problem.
privacy.s1.title: What we collect
privacy.s1.text: Account identifiers (login method and nickname), documents you upload, and operational logs necessary to keep the service running — such as access times, device and browser types, and error information. We do not track your browsing for advertising, and we never use this information for purposes beyond those described here.
privacy.s2.title: How your documents are used
privacy.s2.text: Your documents are only used to build and support your own digital labor. Parsed results are visible only within your account and only to answer your questions; we do not use them for public model training and do not sell them. To complete a request, the necessary content is passed to model and cloud providers (see 'Third-party services').
privacy.s3.title: Storage & security
privacy.s3.text: When accessed over HTTPS, documents are encrypted in transit with TLS; at rest, they are isolated per account with access controls. Operational logs are retained only as long as needed for troubleshooting and are purged automatically.
privacy.s4.title: Third-party services
privacy.s4.text: Parsing and Q&A rely on underlying model and cloud infrastructure providers. We share only the minimum content required to complete each request and require them to uphold equivalent confidentiality.
privacy.s5.title: Your choices
privacy.s5.text: You can view, export, or delete your documents and digital labor at any time. Deleting them also clears the parsed results and generation records. To close your account, contact us and we will process it after verifying your identity.
privacy.s6.title: Minors
privacy.s6.text: This service is intended for users with full civil capacity. If you are under 18, please read this policy and use the service under a guardian's supervision.
privacy.s7.title: Policy updates
privacy.s7.text: If this policy changes materially, we'll post a notice in a prominent place and update the date above. Continued use of the service constitutes acceptance of the updated policy.
terms.s1.title: Service description
terms.s1.text: The service turns the documents and instructions you provide into conversational, task-capable AI Agents (digital labor) in the browser, and provides usage and billing. Outputs are generated automatically; please verify them against the original material.
terms.s2.title: Account & responsibility
terms.s2.text: Keep your account credentials secure; actions under your account are treated as your own. If you notice unusual activity, contact us immediately.
terms.s3.title: Your content
terms.s3.text: You retain all rights to the documents you upload. You also confirm you have lawful rights to use them, and that they do not infringe others' intellectual property, privacy, or other legal rights, nor contain unlawful content.
terms.s4.title: Acceptable use
terms.s4.text: You may not use the service to generate unlawful content, commit fraud, circumvent usage limits, reverse-engineer or stress-test the service, or interfere with its normal operation.
terms.s5.title: Billing & refunds
terms.s5.text: Fees are based on the credits actually consumed by model calls, plus any one-off service fees for publishing or exporting as configured; the page and actual usage are the source of truth. If the service is unavailable due to our own fault, you may request a corresponding refund.
terms.s6.title: Changes & termination
terms.s6.text: We may adjust, suspend, or terminate features, with advance notice for material changes. If you disagree, you may stop using the service and delete your data.
terms.s7.title: Disclaimer
terms.s7.text: The service is provided "as is." AI output does not constitute legal, medical, financial, or other professional advice; consult qualified professionals for such matters.
terms.s8.title: Governing law
terms.s8.text: These terms are governed by the laws of the People's Republic of China. In case of dispute, the parties shall first attempt amicable resolution.

skillCall.title: Skill calling: no commands to write — just direct your AI.
skillCall.desc: TransWeb Skills is an open-source set of Agent Skills. No terminal, no commands to remember: hand the repository to an AI assistant that supports SKILL.md (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, DSH, OpenClaw), or open the published “TransWeb AI Apps” skill in WorkBuddy. The AI handles installation, configuration, and calls for you.
skillCall.prompt.label: SAY TO YOUR AI
skillCall.1.title: Let your AI install it
skillCall.1.text: Send the repository URL (or the source ZIP) to your AI. It pulls the repo and installs transweb-ai; ask it to add transweb-create when you want to create new skills. No terminal to open, no install commands to remember.
skillCall.1.prompt: “Please install the transweb-ai skill. If it is already installed, check that it is complete and working.”
skillCall.2.title: Let your AI connect the key
skillCall.2.text: Generate an ak_live_... key in the account menu on transweb.cn and paste it to your AI. It writes the local config and runs a self-check; no files to edit, no commands to run.
skillCall.2.prompt: “Use the transweb-ai skill to set up my transweb.cn API key. I will paste the key to you.”
skillCall.3.title: Just assign the work
skillCall.3.text: After that, brief it like a colleague. Chain several skills together: Agent apps return text, Skill apps return a result link.
